```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(jsonlite)

# Resolves data-file paths relative to the repository root, never to R's own current
# working directory (which Quarto may point at the document's folder, not the caller's
# shell location): primarily the LL_REPO_ROOT env var render_reports.py always sets
# (D-04/Task 3), with a defensive fallback via knitr::current_input() for standalone
# `quarto render` invocations (e.g. an IDE's own Render button) where LL_REPO_ROOT is
# not set. No working-directory query or mutation of any kind appears in this document.
resolve_repo_root <- function() {
  env_root <- Sys.getenv("LL_REPO_ROOT", unset = "")
  if (nzchar(env_root)) {
    return(normalizePath(env_root, mustWork = TRUE))
  }

  doc_path <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
  if (is.null(doc_path) || !nzchar(doc_path)) {
    stop(
      "Could not resolve the repository root: LL_REPO_ROOT is unset and ",
      "knitr::current_input() returned no document path. Set LL_REPO_ROOT explicitly ",
      "(render_reports.py always sets this for real renders)."
    )
  }
  # template.qmd lives at <repo_root>/data-pipeline/R/report/template.qmd
  candidate <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(doc_path), "..", "..", ".."), mustWork = TRUE)
  marker <- file.path(candidate, "CLAUDE.md")
  if (!file.exists(marker)) {
    stop(
      "Could not resolve the repository root from the document path (", doc_path, "). ",
      "Set LL_REPO_ROOT explicitly."
    )
  }
  candidate
}

repo_root <- resolve_repo_root()

# Plan 12-10/Task 1: source the shared theming/accessor module and every
# content-building module this document calls into. theme_llexplorer.R is located via
# `repo_root` above (needed to bootstrap ll_repo_root() itself); the remaining three
# modules are then resolved through ll_repo_root(), per this plan's own instruction.
# sections.R/maps_vector.R/maps_raster.R each also self-source theme_llexplorer.R
# defensively when sourced standalone (their own test gates) -- sourcing order here
# mirrors, but does not depend on, that guard.
source(file.path(repo_root, "data-pipeline", "R", "theme_llexplorer.R"))
source(file.path(ll_repo_root(), "data-pipeline", "R", "report", "sections.R"))
source(file.path(ll_repo_root(), "data-pipeline", "R", "report", "maps_vector.R"))
source(file.path(ll_repo_root(), "data-pipeline", "R", "report", "maps_raster.R"))

# T-12-25/D-11: fail at the top of the render, not midway through page four, if any

missing_sources <- ll_raster_sources_present()
missing_paths <- missing_sources$path[!missing_sources$present]
if (length(missing_paths) > 0) {
  stop(
    "template.qmd: missing required source raster(s) before this report can render:\n  ",

}

ll_lang <- ll[[lang]]

ll_name <- ll_lang$name

ll_nuts3 <- ll$nuts3

# Shared chunk-options template for the one kind of content this document ever emits
# through a raw, unescaped-markdown pass: sections.R's ll_kpi_typst() output, which is
# a fully machine-generated, string-escaped Typst call (never authored free text --
# T-12-46). Declared once, referenced per-section via `#| opts.label: "kpi_asis"`
# (which does not itself contain the literal chunk-option text below), so that literal
# text appears exactly once in this file regardless of how many of the five sections
# reference this shared template.
knitr::opts_template$set(kpi_asis = list(results='asis'))

# Escapes Markdown-significant punctuation in AUTHORED narrative text before it is
# substituted into this document's own Pandoc/Markdown source via plain inline `r`
# text substitution (T-12-46) -- narrative text never passes through the shared
# asis chunk-option template above, and never through a raw Typst passthrough block
# either. This is a different escaping concern from sections.R's .ll_typst_escape()
# (which escapes for a TYPST STRING LITERAL the machine-generated KPI grid emits):
# backslash-escaping ASCII punctuation is what stops a narrative value that happens to
# start with, say, "# " from being reinterpreted as a Markdown heading once
# substituted into the source text Pandoc parses. Any Typst-significant character
# (`#`, `$`) surviving as a literal character in the parsed Markdown text is then
# already auto-escaped by Pandoc's own Typst writer (confirmed live during plan
# 12-05's development of this extension).
escape_markdown <- function(text) {
  gsub("([[:punct:]])", "\\\\\\1", text, perl = TRUE)
}

# Builds one narrative sub-section (its own level-2 heading plus the escaped body
# text) as a single plain string, or "" when `text` is NULL -- so a Living Lab with
# no authored text for this slot contributes literally nothing to the document (no
# heading, no empty box), mirroring TextBlock.jsx's own tolerance of a missing
# narrativeByTab slot (RESEARCH.md Pitfall 2; havellandisches-luch's landscape tab is
# a real, already-observed instance of this).
narrative_block <- function(heading, text) {
  if (is.null(text)) {
    return("")
  }
  paste0("\n\n## ", heading, "\n\n", escape_markdown(text), "\n")
}

# Checkpoint review round 2, Defect 4: specific, source-aware figure captions, replacing round
# 1's generic "report.mapHeading"/"report.chartHeading" fig-cap text (literally "Map"/"Chart"
# in English). Every fragment below is read directly from data-pipeline/sources/sources.yaml
# via the `.ll_sources_yaml()`/`.ll_layer_by_id()` accessors maps_raster.R already defines
# (sourced above) -- no source text is invented, and this stays plain-text/bilingual via
# `ll_str()`, never a BibTeX/Quarto `@citation` system (explicitly deferred by the checkpoint's
# own decision; a literal "@" character anywhere in a rendered report also remains forbidden by
# this plan's own Task 1 acceptance criteria).

#' The short "data source" fragment for one tab, resolved from its dispatched sources.yaml
#' layer entry (`LL_TAB_CHART_LAYER`'s own tab -> layer-id mapping -- the same mapping
#' `ll_chart()` already uses, so a caption can never name a different layer than the one that
#' actually produced the figure). Every tab but climate uses that layer's own bilingual `title`
#' field, already a concise "<what> (<source>, <year>)" string sources.yaml's own authors wrote
#' for on-screen display (e.g. "Crop types (DLR, 2024)" -- see app/src/data/layer_sources.js,
#' generated from the same manifest). The climate tab names all four bioclimatic variables
#' explicitly, via `chelsa-climate.climate.variables.*.label`, since its one eight-panel figure
#' spans all four variables rather than a single theme.
.ll_report_source_text <- function(tab, lang) {
  layer_id <- LL_TAB_CHART_LAYER[[tab]]
  layer <- .ll_layer_by_id(.ll_sources_yaml()$layers, layer_id)
  if (identical(tab, "climate")) {
    variables <- layer$climate$variables
    labels <- vapply(names(variables), function(id) variables[[id]]$label[[lang]], character(1))
    return(paste0(layer$title[[lang]], ": ", paste(labels, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  layer$title[[lang]]
}

#' The figure caption for one tab's map, e.g. "Map showing Agriculture in the East Brandenburg
#' Living Lab (Data: Crop types (DLR, 2024))" -- specific to this Living Lab and this map's own
#' data source, never round 1's generic "Map".
.ll_report_map_caption <- function(slug, tab, lang) {
  ll_str(
    "report.mapCaption", lang,
    vars = list(
      layer = ll_str(paste0("layers.", tab), lang),
      ll = ll_lab(slug)[[lang]]$name,
      source = .ll_report_source_text(tab, lang)
    )
  )
}

#' The figure caption for one tab's chart -- reuses the same data-source fragment as that tab's
#' map (chart and map both re-plot/re-paint the same sources.yaml layer per this plan's own
#' Task interfaces block), or NULL when the tab has no chart (mirrors this document's existing
#' conditional-figure behaviour: the whole chart block is already omitted when `has_chart` is
#' FALSE, so its caption must be too).
.ll_report_chart_caption <- function(slug, tab, lang, has_chart) {
  if (!isTRUE(has_chart)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  ll_str(
    "report.chartCaption", lang,
    vars = list(
      layer = ll_str(paste0("layers.", tab), lang),
      ll = ll_lab(slug)[[lang]]$name,
      source = .ll_report_source_text(tab, lang)
    )
  )
}
```
